newsitem.title: USA: Investor Michael Price takes stake in Reader's Digest.
newsitem.headline: Investor Michael Price takes stake in Reader's Digest.

text.p: Money manager Michael Price said Monday he has accumulated a stake of about 700,000 shares of Reader's Digest Association Inc., the troubled publisher that is looking for a new chief executive.

Price, chairman of the Franklin Mutual Advisers mutual fund group, has taken major positions in stocks he considered undervalued and has actively pressured the management of those companies to find ways to boost the stock price.
One of those stocks was Chase Manhattan Corp., which merged with Manufacturers Hanover last year. Price had bought a large stake in Chase and helped pressure the bank to improve its share price.
Price said he accumulated the Readers Digest stake, equal to about 0.7 percent of the company's stock, in the last few months but had not bought any shares in recent weeks.
The company said a week ago that Chief Executive James Schadt resigned after three years of sluggish profits and a sliding stock price.

Price said he was drawn to the stock on expectation that the DeWitt Wallace Reader's Digest Fund and the Lila Wallace Reader's Digest Fund, which together own about 72 percent of the company, would reduce their holdings to about 50 percent by the year 2000 to avoid substantial excise taxes.
"They're going to have to find a home for stock," said Price. "They should get the stock up before."
Price said he didn't expect a rapid turnaround. The CEO search will take about two to three months, and the new chief will need about another six months "to get his feet on the ground," he said.
Price said the company has a "fabulous brand name, a great franchise, with great assets" in its mailing lists and other areas.
Still, analysts said Price would only be able to bring limited pressure on the company.

"He can only do it through the powers of persuasion for the next few years," said independent analyst J. Kendrick Noble. "His interests are with those of (the foundations). He can persuade (management), but he really can't force any course of action for the foreseeable future."
Readers Digest stock rose $1 to $27.44 on the New York Stock Exchange. The company has about 106 million shares outstanding.

The company said Friday it hired an executive search firm to help find a new CEO, a day after it said it lost $23 million in the latest quarter as it tried to revamp its businesses. The publisher also warned that 1998 results would be weaker than 1997 results.
In June, Price bought a chunk of Dow Jones & Co. stock from money manager James Cramer, bringing his stake to about 4.6 million shares.

Price said at the time he expected Dow Jones to sell or spin off its troubled electronic information unit, Dow Jones Markets. Dow Jones has said it would keep the unit and invest up to $650 million over three years to strengthen it.
